card.statement:
The centraliser $\mathfrak{g}^{e}$ has a basis consisting of elements

(4.9)

$\{c_{a,i,b,k}^{(r)}\mid 1\leq a,b\leq m,1\leq i\leq\nu_{a},1\leq k\leq\nu_{b}, s_{a,b}\leq r

and the Lie bracket is given by

(4.10)

$[c_{a,i,b,j}^{(r)},c_{c,k,d,l}^{(s)}]=\delta_{b,c}\delta_{j,k}c_{a,i,d,l}^{(r+s)}-\delta_{a,d}\delta_{i,l}c_{c,k,b,j}^{(r+s)}.$

Furthermore $\mathfrak{g}^{e}$ is a Dynkin graded subalgebra of $\mathfrak{g}$ with $c_{a,i,b,k}^{(r)}$ lying in degree $2r$. $\hfill\qed$

4.2. Symplectic and orthogonal subalgebras

Fix $N>0$ an integer and $\varepsilon=\pm 1$ such that $\varepsilon^{N}=1$. We keep the partition $\lambda$ and shift matrix $\sigma$ from Section 4.1, and we now also assume that $\lambda\in\mathcal{P}_{\varepsilon}(N)$ and that $\nu$ is $(-\varepsilon(-1)^{\lambda_{1}},\sigma)$ -admissible.

Consider the matrix

(4.11)

$\displaystyle J:=\sum_{a=1}^{m}\sum_{i=1}^{\nu_{a}}\sum_{j=1}^{\lambda(\nu)_{a}}(\beta)^{i}(-1)^{j+1}e_{a,i,j;a,\nu_{a}+1-i,\lambda(\nu)_{a}+1-j}$

This is a block diagonal matrix can be described as follows. For each index $a=1,...,m$ there is a block of size $\nu_{a}\lambda(\nu)_{a}$, and each of these blocks is an antidiagonal matrix with entries $\pm 1$. Furthermore, when $\varepsilon=1$ the matrix $J$ is symmetric and when $\varepsilon=-1$ it is anti-symmetric.

Now define an involution of $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{gl}_{N}$ by the rule

(4.12)

$\displaystyle\tau:X\mapsto-J^{-1}X^{\top}J$

We decompose $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{g}_{0}\oplus\mathfrak{g}_{1}$ into eigenspaces for $\tau$ so that $\mathfrak{g}_{0}$ is the space of $\tau$ -invariants. Note that $J$ is symmetric and $\mathfrak{g}_{0}\cong\mathfrak{so}_{N}$ for $\varepsilon=1$, whilst $J$ is antisymmetric and $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{sp}_{N}$ for $\varepsilon=-1$.

By Lemma 4.2(ii) we have $\{e,h\}\subseteq\mathfrak{g}_{0}$, whilst $f\in\mathfrak{g}_{0}$ thanks to [CM93, Lemma 3.4.4]. Write $G_{0}$ for the connected component of the subgroup of $\operatorname{GL}_{N}$ consisting of elements which preserve the bilinear form associated to $J$, so that $G_{0}$ is connected and $\operatorname{Lie}(G_{0})=\mathfrak{g}_{0}$.
card.label: Lemma 4.1

paper.title: Shifted twisted Yangians and Slodowy slices in classical Lie algebras
paper.abstract: In this paper we introduce the shifted twisted Yangian of type {\sf AI}, following the work of Lu--Wang--Zhang, and we study their semiclassical limits, a class of Poisson algebras. We demonstrate that they coincide with the Dirac reductions of the semiclassical shifted Yangian for $\mathfrak{gl}_n$. We deduce that these shifted twisted Yangians admit truncations which are isomorphic to Slodowy slices for many non-rectangular nilpotent elements in types {\sf B}, {\sf C}, {\sf D}. As a direct consequence we obtain parabolic presentations of the semiclassical shifted twisted Yangian, analogous to those introduced by Brundan--Kleshchev for the Yangian of type {\sf A}. Finally we give Poisson presentations of Slodowy slices for all even nilpotent elements in types {\sf B}, {\sf C}, {\sf D}, generalising the recent work of the second author.
